name: Plus Plug S
config_flow_sub_profile_remarks:
You need to select a profile depending on your settings.
The ECO setting (`Sys` `device.eco_mode`, an experimental mode that throttles the CPU and uses the wireless low-power mode) only changes the power consumption in the listed configurations. Activating any other settings not listed in the profile name will change the power draw.

LED status indicator variants (`PLUGS_UI` `leds.mode`):
- "LED": `leds.mode = "switch"`, i.e. the LED follows the output state. `colors.switch:0.on` = rgb [0, 100, 0] at brightness 100, `colors.switch:0.off` = rgb [100, 0, 0] at brightness 100, so the LED is lit in both states. Night mode disabled.
- "No LED": `leds.mode = "off"`, LED indication disabled completely.

The factory default is `leds.mode = "power"`, where the LED colour follows the measured power. That mode was not measured separately. Because it keeps the LED lit in both relay states, pick one of the `+LED` sub-profiles if you did not change the LED setting; pick a variant without LED if you switched the indication off.

Sub-profile configurations:
"WLAN + BT + ECO": All three turned on.
"WLAN + ECO": Both turned on.
"WLAN + BT": Both turned on, ECO turned off.
"WLAN": Only WLAN turned on, ECO turned off.
description: Smart Wi-Fi Plug with Power Monitoring
measure_description:
Two measurement setups are combined in this profile.

The root `standby_power` (0.74 W) and `standby_power_on` (1.01 W) are the original values: manually measured with a GW Instek GPM-8310, LED off, and transcribed from https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cLtao6yG7ds. V2 was added to V1 because the manufacturer does not mention changes other than mechanical. They are kept unchanged for existing installations until a sub-profile is selected; the `measure_device` field names the meter used for the eight sub-profiles below.

The eight sub-profiles were measured with a Shelly Plug S Gen3: the plug under test and a calibrated resistive dummy load are connected in parallel to the same mains input, and the Shelly measures upstream of both. The dummy load is never connected to the relay output, so the reference meter always sees the plug plus the dummy load and can resolve the sub-watt self-consumption. Its contribution is subtracted per sample as V^2/R instead of a fixed offset, because it follows the mains voltage. The stored sub-profile values are time averages over the measurement window of each state, not peak values. Plug firmware version 1.7.6.
